newsitem.title: USA: Israelis said to rebuff U.S pressure on Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israelis said to rebuff U.S pressure on Hebron.

text.p: Israel on Tuesday rebuffed U.S. efforts at the Middle East crisis summit to pin down a date for a military withdrawal from the West Bank city of Hebron, Israeli official Natan Sharansky said.

"Definitely it was clear the American side wants ... to set a final date. We were saying it is impossible," Sharansky, Israel's trade minister and a member of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's delegation told reporters.

The status of Israeli troops in Hebron, the last and most sensitive of West Bank cities once occupied by Israel, is a key part of current Israeli-Palestinian frictions because Israel has refused to carry out an earlier partial-pullback agreement.

Sharansky also said Netanyahu had rejected a proposal that non-stop negotiations on a Hebron redeployment -- something he himself had proposed for after the Washington summit -- begin right away in Washington. He stuck to his position that such talks begin later.

The Washington meeting began Tuesday and was expected to conclude on Wednesday. Tuesday's meetings included separate Clinton talks with Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat, a group meeting of those three and Jordan's King Hussein and a long private discussion between Netanyahu and Arafat.
